dedupe_keys.name: citizen science method for infiltration and flood resilience of urban green spaces birmingham london chantilly frontiers in water 2021

description: This methods study tests whether citizen scientists can assess the flood mitigation potential of urban green spaces by measuring soil infiltration rate and simple soil characteristics. Earthwatch Europe ran it with Imperial College London, Royal Holloway University of London and the University of Siena, and published it in Frontiers in Water on 15 April 2021. Coverage is managed and unmanaged green spaces in Birmingham, London and Chantilly in France, sampled by volunteers in 30 events over 2018 and 2019. Infiltration was best predicted by soil compaction, soil colour, air temperature and insolation, and the authors built and validated a classification flow diagram so volunteers can rate sites as high or low infiltration. Format and access: an open access article with tables of model coefficients and colour thresholds. Licence: CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: the raw volunteer measurements are not published as a data set, and thresholds are tuned to temperate cities. It supports climate adaptation planning of green infrastructure for pluvial flooding. Related catalogue records are the Earthwatch FreshWater Watch data set and the BGS Infiltration SuDS Map.
